droṇakalaśa
------------------------------------------
Among the वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, the Somayāgas are a class by themselves. The सोम juice is the main द्रव्य or ingredient to be offered into the sacrificial fire in these yāgas. The सोम juice is prepared by crushing the सोम stalks with stones. It is then strained through a cloth called दशापवित्र into a wooden vessel with a handle. This latter is called ‘droṇakalaśa’ or ‘duroṇakalaśa’.
See DAŚĀPAVITRA also.

Droṇācārya
------------------------------------------
Bhīṣma and Droṇa or द्रोणाचार्य were the two greatest warriors that fought for दुर्योधन in the कुरुक्षेत्र war of the Mahābhārata. Like परशुराम, his teacher, द्रोणाचार्य too was a ब्राह्मण by birth, but a क्षत्त्रिय (warrior) by profession.
Born as the son of the sage भरद्वाज, he got his early एदुचतिओन्, including the training in dhanurvidyā or archery from the ṛṣi अग्निवेश. Drupada, the king of Pāñcāla, was a fellow-student. After completing his training under अग्नि-veśa, he once approached the king Drupada for financial help. The king in his arrogance humiliated him. Enraged by this, he approached परशुराम for higher training in archery and warfare so that he could take revenge on the king. After completing the same, he was, though by chance, appointed as the teacher of the Kaurava and the Pāṇḍava princes by भीष्म. अर्जुन, of the five Pāṇḍava princes, proved to be his worthiest and best disciple. With his help, he got Drupada taken prisoner, usurped half of his kingdom and then let him off.
Once, the Pāṇḍava princes discovered the hunter-boy एकलव्य in a forest by accident and found him to be a better archer than अर्जुन. एकलव्य claimed to be a disciple of द्रोणाचार्य himself. The latter then demanded and got his thumb as his गुरुदक्षिणा or fee just to please अर्जुन!
Throughout the conflict between the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas, द्रोणाचार्य too, like भीष्म, tried his best to advise दुर्योधन to desist from his evil ways and make peace with the Pāṇḍavas. But his advice fell on deaf ears.
In the ensuing कुरुक्षेत्र war he fought fiercely, first under भीष्म and later as the commander-in-chief. Then as per the advice of the sages like वसिष्ठ and गौतम, he retired from the battle and sat in योग. At that time he was killed by धृष्टद्युम्न, the son of Drupada.
Two more Droṇas are mentioned in the पुराणस्. One was a Vasu (a kind of a demigod) who, along with his wife Dharā, performed austerities in the गन्ध-mādana hill for long time to get the Lord as their son. They were reborn as नन्द and यशोदा in their next life. Lord कृष्ण, as their foster child, gave them great happiness and bliss through his childish pranks.
The sage Śārṅgaka, the son of the sage Mandapāla and Jaritā when they had assumed the bodies of birds, was also known as Droṇa and was considered a ब्रह्मर्षि.
Droṇa is also the name of a mountain mentioned in some पुराणस्.

Droṇaparva
------------------------------------------
The seventh book of the Mahā-bhārata, each of which is known as a parva (a knot or a joint or a book), the द्रोणपर्व contains the exploits of the teacher द्रोणाचार्य until his death at the hands of धृष्टद्युम्न, the commander-in-chief of the Pāṇḍava army.
See also DROṆĀCĀRYA and MAHĀ-BHĀRATA.
